items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: I had the good fortune of being on his staff along with Billy May

ctx.x: To begin with, until I got a clear picture of the keyboard in my mind, and in fact, I think I told you a little story over this one time. I used to walk down the street, you know, I'd get to hummin' a riff, a picture where it would be, and I'd walk down with my hands stretched, with my five fingers out, I'd say well, here's five lines, and four spaces and this thing, and I was walking down the street one day, and a lady looked at me as if I were crazy, you know,

and all of a sudden I realized, and I turned around to her, and I said, 'Lady, I'm not crazy. I'm just picturing a musical version.' It was funny. So I quit that. At that time it helped me to concentrate, you know, to picture. So now I can do it without the piano. In fact, it's been quite a few years; I can do it without (unintelligible). Every now and then I might want to check some. I'll get stuck, if it's something difficult, you know, maybe difficult chord or one of those things. I might just play it. Go to…
